To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spatial cueing (reflexive) effect depends on shape similarities between cue and target.
the spatial cueing effects depend on the shapes of cue and target stimuli.

(1) the spatial cueing effects depend on the shapes of both the cue and the subsequent target; and (2) a simple neural network model can explain these findings, suggesting that reflexive attention effects can be distributed throughout the visual brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of stimulus shape on the spatial attentional effects.
the effects of shape similarity on reflexive attention.
the neural mechanisms of reflexive attention and the role of shape similarity in the reflexive spatial attention.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neural mechanism of the spatial cue is not the same as the neural mechanism of spatial attention, but the neural mechanisms of the spatial cue and of the target are similar.
shape similarity between the cue and target can affect the spatial cueing and the spatial cueing is affected by the shape similarity between cue and target.
the spatial cueing is a result of the interaction of the spatial and the non-spatial attentional systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reflexive attention is a distributed process that depends on the similarity of the cue and target stimuli.
shape information can be used as a spatial cue to guide spatial attention, and the spatial cueing mechanism can be used to guide shape selection.
reflexive attention can be modulated by stimulus attributes and the spatial cueing effects can be explained by the repetition suppression of neuronal responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
reflexive attention is a general mechanism that is modulated by the properties of the visual stimuli and not a specialized mechanism that is only expressed in a specific region of the brain.
shape information can be used to modulate the reflexive orienting of attention.
the spatial cueing effects and their dependence on the shape similarity between cue and target can be explained with a single model.
